card: A stock room and lending desk: catalogue, QR labels, photo-evidence loans, stock counts and transfers between spaces.
name: Space Works Inventory
title: Open-source makerspace inventory & lending | Space Works
description: Space Works Inventory is free, open-source, self-hosted inventory and tool lending software for makerspaces, tool libraries and fab labs, with QR labels.
definition: Space Works Inventory is a free, open-source, self-hosted stock room and lending desk for makerspaces, tool libraries and fab labs that tracks stock, lends tools with a QR scan and moves stock between rooms or makerspaces.
summary: Space Works Inventory keeps the catalogue, shelves and bins in order, lends tools to members with a QR scan and a photo at every handover, counts stock and moves it between rooms or between makerspaces, all on infrastructure you control. One installation runs several makerspaces, each with its own members, roles, settings and audit trail. It is fully standalone, and its REST API and signed webhooks connect it to the other Space Works apps or anything else.
stack: Next.js 16, React, Prisma, PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7, BullMQ, Silo object storage, Caddy, Docker Compose (Node 22)
relationship: Fully standalone with its own installation and database. Its REST API and signed webhooks connect it to the other Space Works apps (Events, Workspace, Bookings, Machines) or anything else. Its inventory, lending and transfer domain is ported from the original Space Works makerspace manager.

features.heading: Set up in minutes
items: A first-run wizard for the admin, your first makerspace, locations, categories, units, roles, lending and fees.
Locations nest from building to room to shelf to bin.
Bulk import from CSV or Excel with a validated preview, templates and a realistic sample inventory.

features.heading: Catalogue and stock
items: Quantity-tracked items and serialized assets, with photos, suppliers, costs and per-item lending rules.
QR labels for items, assets, shelves, kits and containers, printed as PDF sheets in three sizes.
Receipts, adjustments with a reason, moves between shelves, a repair shelf and an append-only stock ledger.
Cycle counts, blind if you like, scheduled or ad hoc, with four-eyes posting above a threshold.
Low-stock alerts, a to-buy list and stock valuation at weighted average cost.

features.heading: Transfers between rooms and makerspaces
items: Request, approve, pick and dispatch with QR scans, then receive in one go or in parts.
Move stock between locations of a space or between makerspaces of the same installation.
Damaged units go to the repair shelf, missing units are declared and refused units return to the sender.
Stock stays correct in transit, and both spaces see the full timeline.

features.heading: Lending
items: A member catalogue and an optional public one, with requests, staff approval, renewals and self-checkout.
Guided issue and return desk flows: scan labels, check lines, add photos and remarks.
Overdue reminders and escalation; lost or damaged items open incidents that can restrict borrowing.
Free or paid lending: deposits, daily, weekly or flat rental, late fees and damage or loss charges.

features.heading: Repairs and finance
items: Report damaged items, keep a technician directory and send repair requests by email, WhatsApp or Telegram.
External technicians get a private link; staff verify fixes and pay them.
One finance ledger for payments, refunds, payouts and purchases, with CSV or Excel downloads.

features.heading: Roles, reports and integrations
items: Roles for Inventory manager, Staff, Member and Technician, with every settings change audited.
Reports with CSV and Excel exports, an audit log, and email and in-app notifications.
A REST API with API keys and signed outbound webhooks.
Email and password, emailed magic links and authenticator-app MFA.

faqs.q: Is Space Works Inventory free?
faqs.a: Yes. Space Works Inventory is free, open-source software under the GNU AGPL v3.0 or later, so you can use, study, change and share it, including for your own makerspace.

faqs.q: Can I self-host Space Works Inventory?
faqs.a: Yes. Space Works Inventory installs on your own 64-bit Linux server with one curl command and runs with PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7, Silo object storage and Caddy for automatic HTTPS. An optional cloud setup runs on free plans with Render and managed services.

faqs.q: Can Space Works Inventory charge for tool loans?
faqs.a: Yes, lending can be free or paid. Space Works Inventory supports refundable deposits, rental fees, late fees and damage or loss charges; members pay with Razorpay or Stripe, staff record cash or bank payments, or members choose pay later.

faqs.q: Can one Space Works Inventory install run several makerspaces?
faqs.a: Yes. One installation of Space Works Inventory runs several makerspaces, each with its own members, roles, settings and audit trail, and stock can be transferred between them.

faqs.q: Does Space Works Inventory work with the main Space Works platform?
faqs.a: Space Works Inventory is fully standalone with its own installation. Its REST API and signed webhooks connect it to the other Space Works apps (Events, Workspace, Bookings and Machines) or anything else.

card: 3D printers, laser cutters and CNC: job requests with a fair queue, pricing and payments, consumables, repairs and maintenance.

category: Machine and 3D print job management software
title: Open-source makerspace machine management | Space Works
description: Space Works Machines is free, open-source, self-hosted machine management for makerspaces and fab labs: 3D print and laser job queues, payments and maintenance.
h1: Machine and job management for makerspaces
definition: Space Works Machines is a free, open-source, self-hosted machine management app for makerspaces, fab labs and college workshops that runs job requests through a fair queue, takes payments and tracks consumables, maintenance and repairs.
summary: Space Works Machines lists your 3D printers, laser cutters, CNC routers and the rest, takes job requests with files and a fair queue, prices them or keeps them free, and takes payments online or at the desk. Consumables, maintenance, faults and warranties sit in one place, and printers and other tools can connect through a REST API and webhooks. One install runs many makerspaces, each with its own staff, makers, machines, prices and payment account, and your makers' data stays in your own database.
stack: Next.js 16, React, Prisma, PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7, BullMQ, Silo object storage, Caddy, Docker Compose (Node 22)
relationship: A separate self-hosted app with its own installer and database. Its rules for machines, printing, maintenance and payments are ported from the Django Space Works apps, and it connects to printers and other tools through a REST API and signed webhooks.

features.heading: Machines and the public catalogue
items: Machine types for FDM and resin printers, laser cutters, CNC routers and mills, vinyl cutters, PCB mills and more.
Each type sets its own spec fields, request fields, file rules, materials and colours.
Machine records with photos, manuals, SOPs, safety sheets and a status that always carries a word.
A public catalogue per space that never shows notes, costs, serial numbers or meters.

features.heading: Jobs, from request to collection
items: Makers request a job with files checked against the machine type's rules.
STL and G-code files are parsed for size and slicer estimates.
A fair queue with positions and an estimated wait.
Approve, start, pause, complete, fail, collect and reprint, with a timeline and a private status link.
Consumables are reserved when a job starts and reconciled when it finishes.

features.heading: Prices and payments
items: Free, flat, time, material or time and material pricing, with member and public rates, minimum charges and tax.
Payment upfront, on completion with an optional deposit, or pay later.
Each space's own Razorpay or Stripe account, or desk payments by cash, UPI, bank transfer or card terminal.
Refunds for rejected, cancelled and failed jobs follow your rules, including partial refunds.

features.heading: Consumables, upkeep and repairs
items: Consumable pools for filament, resin and sheets, with an append-only ledger and low-stock alerts.
Maintenance schedules by date, machine hours or job count, with reminders.
Fault reports, downtime windows, warranties with expiry reminders and a service history per machine.
Ask several technicians at once by email, WhatsApp or Telegram; the first to accept takes the repair.

features.heading: Reports and finance
items: Reports on jobs, utilisation, MTBF, MTTR, consumables, revenue, maintenance and repair spend.
CSV and Excel export for every report.
An append-only finance ledger with money in, out and net by day, week, month or financial year.
Money is visible to the machine manager only.

features.heading: Connections and accounts
items: A REST API at /api/v1 with per-space keys and scopes, and an OpenAPI document.
Signed outbound webhooks with retries and a delivery log.
Printer connections today: manual and a built-in simulated printer. OctoPrint, Moonraker/Klipper, Bambu Lab and PrusaLink are coming soon.
Team chat alerts to Slack, Discord, Mattermost, Telegram and WhatsApp.
Six roles from machine manager to maker; staff sign in with an authenticator app.

faqs.q: Is Space Works Machines free?
faqs.a: Yes. Space Works Machines is free, open-source software under the GNU AGPL v3.0 or later, and it is self-hosted, so your makers' data stays in your own database.

faqs.q: Can Space Works Machines take payments for 3D print and laser jobs?
faqs.a: Yes. Space Works Machines prices jobs as free, flat, time, material or time and material, and takes payment through each space's own Razorpay or Stripe account or records it at the desk (cash, UPI, bank transfer or card terminal).

faqs.q: Does Space Works Machines connect to my 3D printers?
faqs.a: Today Space Works Machines offers a manual connection and a built-in simulated printer; OctoPrint, Moonraker/Klipper, Bambu Lab and PrusaLink connections are listed as coming soon. Other tools can connect through its REST API and signed webhooks.

faqs.q: How do I install Space Works Machines?
faqs.a: Run the one-line installer on a Linux server with at least 4 GiB RAM and swap; it checks the server, asks its questions and shows a summary before installing. You can also deploy it to Render with the included Blueprint and your own managed PostgreSQL, Redis, bucket and SMTP.

faqs.q: Does Space Works Machines work with the main Space Works platform?
faqs.a: Space Works Machines is a separate app with its own installer and database. Its rules for machines, printing, maintenance and payments are ported from the Django Space Works apps, and it connects to other systems through a REST API and signed webhooks.

faqs.q: Is Space Works Events free?

faqs.q: Can Space Works Events connect to other systems?

Light and dark themes and Gilroy typography on both platforms.

features.heading: Status and white-labelling
items: Both apps are in development, with no App Store or Google Play release yet.
Debug builds include a labelled demo to try member and staff flows without a backend.
Branding and an optional locked HTTPS server origin are set in branding/brand.json.

faqs.q: Are the Space Works apps on the App Store or Google Play?
faqs.a: Not yet. The Space Works iOS and Android apps are in development with no store releases; Android CI release builds are unsigned and Play distribution still needs owner signing.

faqs.q: Which devices do the Space Works mobile apps support?
faqs.a: The Space Works iOS app targets iOS 17 and later on iPhone and iPad. The Space Works Android app runs on Android 8 (API 26) and later, on phones and tablets.

faqs.q: What do the Space Works mobile apps connect to?
faqs.a: The Space Works mobile apps are clients of a Space Works server through a pinned OpenAPI contract. On iOS you choose a server on launch, or a deployment can lock one HTTPS origin.

faqs.q: Can I try the Space Works mobile apps without a server?
faqs.a: Yes, in Debug builds. Both Space Works apps include a clearly labelled, isolated demo of the member and staff flows; Release builds leave it out.

faqs.q: Can I rebrand the Space Works mobile apps?
faqs.a: Yes. Both Space Works apps read deployment branding and an optional locked HTTPS origin from branding/brand.json, and each has a white-label guide.
